spec.user_stories: - As a rider, I tap the map once to set where I am starting from and tap again to set where I am going. - As a rider, I see a marker at each point I chose so I know what was registered. - As a rider, I can tap a stop dot to use that stop as my point, and hover a dot to see its name. - As a rider, I can press Reset to clear my points and start over. - As a rider, I see a "Find route" button in the side panel.
spec.acceptance_criteria: 1. Scope: only web/index.html, web/map.js, web/style.css change (route lines, stop dots, legend, banner, fitBounds, load failure/empty handling) is unchanged. Pass: git diff touches only those three files, and the map still renders all six routes. 2. First tap on empty map sets origin: one marker appears at the tapped lat/lng. 3. Second tap on empty map sets destination: a second marker appears at the tapped lat/lng; two markers total. 4. Any tap after both points are set (map or stop dot) is ignored: no marker added, none moved. 5. Tapping a stop dot counts as a tap and places the marker at the dot's own position (not the click position), filling origin if empty, else destination. 6. A single dot click creates exactly one marker and advances state by one point (the map click handler does not also fire). 7. Origin and destination markers use the same Leaflet default marker icon, loaded from vendored web/images/ (marker-icon.png / shadow); no request to any third-party host other than OSM tiles. Pass: network panel shows the icon served from the local origin with 200. 8. Hovering a stop dot (mouseover) opens a popup with the stop name; clicking a dot does not depend on a popup to show the name. Pass: popup appears on hover without a click. 9. #panel contains, at the top, two buttons: "Find route" and "Reset", both enabled on page load. 10. Clicking "Find route" does nothing observable: no network request, no DOM change, no state change. 11. Clicking "Reset" removes both markers (or whichever exist) and returns to the "pick origin" state: the next tap sets origin again. Reset with no points set is harmless. 12. After Reset, the full flow (origin, destination, ignore further) works again, repeatedly. 13. No /api/plan call is made(/api/routes, /api/routes/{id}), static assets, and OSM tiles. No loading state, steps list, highlighting, or stop-data storage is added. 14. The banner is not shown, hidden, or cleared by any new behavior (banner logic untouched). 15. No build step, no new files outside the three named (vendored images already exist), no backend or docs changes. 16. pytest is run and its real output (including any failures) is reported; tap behavior is verified manually in a browser since pytest cannot cover it.
spec.assumptions: - OWNER DICEDED: Dragging the map is not a tap; only Leaflet click events count. - OWNER DICEDED: Dots from different routes at the same stop each count as a tap on that dot's own position (same coordinates for a shared stop). - OWNER CONFIRMED: markers are not draggable and have no popup/tooltip. - Layout is desktop only; no responsive CSS. Button styling is minimal and the implementer's call. - The popup-on-hover behavior replaces click-to-open for dots; OWNER DECIDED: the popup closes on mouseout. - Taps on legend/banner/panel are not map taps.
spec.edge_cases: - Tap on a dot while state is "pick destination": sets destination at dot position. - Tap on a dot while both points are set: ignored. - Rapid double-click on the map: may register two taps (origin then destination); Leaflet double-click zoom is left as is (OWNER DECIDED). - Reset immediately followed by a dot click: sets origin at the dot, once. - Origin and destination at the same position (same dot tapped twice): permitted; two markers are placed. - Route data failed to load: no dots exist, but map taps still set points.

risks.risk: Leaflet vector layers (circleMarker) propagate click to the map unless propagation is stopped; a double count is the likely defect and needs manual browser verification.
Default marker icon path auto-detection can break when assets are served from the root; the icon may 404 and must be checked in the network panel.
Origin and destination share one icon, so the user cannot tell which is which; this is an owner decision, accepted.
Tap behavior is untestable by pytest; correctness depends on manual verification.

spec.dependencies: - web/leaflet.js, web/leaflet.css, web/images/marker-icon*.png and marker-shadow.png (already vendored). - Existing code in web/map.js (drawRoute, load) and the empty aside#panel in web/index.html.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria (tap/markers: 2-7; dots: 5, 6, 8; Reset: 11-12; Find route: 9-10). Criteria are observable, though most need a manual browser check. Biggest uncertainty: hover-popup close behavior and double-click timing are unspecified and left to the implementer; neither blocks the spec.
